purpose: Test whether a ceteris-paribus reduction in rooted insurgent armed membership can raise instantaneous recruitment hazard because the eligible pool expands while fielded-force, foothold, and social-access channels remain available.

design.shock_definition: Clone the exact day-60 state and multiply armed_fraction only for members of the canonical insurgent organization. Do not advance time and do not alter formations, foothold strength, social exposure, behavior, grievance, fear, capital, or political access.

primary_outputs: rooted armed membership mass after shock
hazard ratio versus the unshocked state
interpretation: This is a partial-equilibrium diagnostic, not a realistic intervention.
If hazard rises as rooted membership is reduced, Pineland contains an endogenous replacement-pressure mechanism: stock removal expands recruitment eligibility faster than it removes access.

If hazard instead falls, the dynamic day-360 hazard increase in the U replication must come from evolved access, grievance, foothold, or other state changes rather than the immediate eligibility term alone.
guard: Synthetic model mechanism only; no real-world operational claim.
